subject: Stratus MedTech — infra ownership and connectivity snapshot
messages:
From: Dana Singh <dana.singh@stratusmed.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: network+procurement@stratusmed.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Request: governance checklist & network readiness for private deployment

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving ahead on a pilot to run Redwood Private inside our AWS account (VPC, transit, minimal internet egress). Before we go deeper we need a consolidated governance and network readiness artifact for our security/compliance and infra teams. Specifically, they asked for: 

- A single-sheet connectivity diagram that shows peering/Transit Gateway and NAT flow.
- A checklist of commissioning items (IAM roles, service account scopes, KMS key usage, audit log retention).
- Responsible owners from Redwood and Stratus for each gate.

Can you produce a short "snapshot" (1–2 pages) and a commissioning checklist we can give to our cloud infra team? We are under a tight window — procurement would like this by Dec 13th to stay on track for January testing.

Attachments: initial inventory exported from our CMDB (available on request).

Thanks,
Dana Singh
VP, Platform Operations
Stratus MedTech
[Attachment: stratus-cmdb-export.csv (csv)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Dana Singh <dana.singh@stratusmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: governance checklist & network readiness for private deployment

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear ask. We can do a concise snapshot + commissioning checklist and will align owners for each item. Plan I propose: 

1) Deliverable A: Connectivity snapshot (PDF, 1 page) — shows VPC boundaries, peering/transit, NAT/eProxy egress, and KMS location.
2) Deliverable B: Commissioning checklist (XLSX) — concrete gate items with owners and verification steps.
3) Deliverable C: Short runbook for temporary access (jumpbox, SRE bastion rules) and audit-log evidence locations.

Request from your side: please confirm the AWS account ID and whether you plan to use Transit Gateway or VPC peering for isolation. That determines routing and NAT placement. Also confirm if you require HSM-backed KMS (we support both).

I will attach our first-draft network diagram and the checklist template — Ben will add technical notes on firewall/NAT rules.

Can we aim to deliver the snapshot + checklist by EOD Dec 10? That gives you two days to circulate.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-diagram-v1.pdf (pdf, 2 pages)]
[Attachment: commissioning-checklist-v2.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dana Singh <dana.singh@stratusmed.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: governance checklist & network readiness for private deployment

Rafael — adding a few technical clarifications I want reflected in the checklist/template: 

- Preferred topology: Transit Gateway with route table per tenant is the recommended pattern when customers expect multiple subnets and cross-account peering later. If Stratus prefers a single-VPC pilot, make NAT placement explicit (public NAT instance vs managed NAT gateway) and expected egress bandwidth.
- Egress rules: Redwood recommends allowing outbound to our control-plane endpoints over 443 + static IP ranges (we'll provide a small list). Avoid opening broad 0.0.0.0/0 to management ports.
- Service accounts: we need an IAM role that allows AssumeRole with a restricted policy that only permits S3:GetObject (for log retrieval) and KMS:Decrypt on the keys you designate.
- KMS: if you require KMS-HSM, call that out — it changes key policy language and requires provisioning lead time.

I've annotated the diagram with suggested NAT/gateway placement and added a short snippet for the role policy under the "Access gates" section in the checklist.

Small ask for your procurement/security review: can you confirm audit log retention target (e.g., 90/180/365 days) and whether logs are stored in your central logging account or per-tenant bucket? That will affect the runbook for evidence collection.

Thanks — I can circulate an updated diagram (v2) with those notes.

—Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Inline: quoted earlier messages]

> Hi Dana — thanks for the clear ask....

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Singh <dana.singh@stratusmed.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Snapshot deliverable + ownership matrix — ready for customer handoff

Team — attaching the finalized snapshot we will hand to the Stratus infra team today. Summary below for quick reference.

Key points (one-line):
- Topology: Transit Gateway chosen by Stratus; TGW route tables per environment (pilot/prod). NAT: managed NAT Gateway in a dedicated public subnet.
- KMS: Stratus requested HSM-backed keys for patient-data-encryption; Marissa to confirm onboarding steps with Customer Success + Security.
- Audit logs: Stratus confirmed 365-day retention in their central logging account; Redwood will provide S3 object prefixes for our service logs.

Activation ownership matrix (owners and verification step):
- TGW peering & route tables: Stratus infra (Dana) — verify by traceroute to control-plane IPs and by checking route table entries.
- NAT & egress policy: Stratus infra (Dana) + Redwood network engineer (Ben) — verify by sample outbound tokenized requests and egress IP validation.
- IAM role & access policy: Kimberly Park (Redwood) — verify AssumeRole and minimal permissions via test harness.
- KMS/HSM provisioning: Marissa Cole (Redwood CS) + Stratus security — verify key policy and test encryption/decryption cycle.
- Audit-log handoff & retention evidence: Stratus infra (Dana) — provide S3 lifecycle policy screenshot and example log object paths.

Next steps for today:
1) I'll send the snapshot + checklist to Dana and procurement and request confirmation of the account ID and TGW attachment ARN.
2) Ben, please prepare a short verification runbook (5 steps) we can paste in the commissioning checklist under "validation tests".
3) Kimberly, prepare the minimal IAM JSON we can paste into the checklist.

If we have confirmation from Dana by EOD Dec 13, procurement stays on schedule. Good work team.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-diagram-v1.pdf (pdf, final annotated)]
